classification.difficultyReason: Interpret a tidal chart, estimate extrema and identify an approximate period.

content.prompt: A tidal chart is shown below.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5 tidal chart above part a
spec.description: Three-day tidal-height chart with hourly grid divisions, three-hour time labels, day spans and unequal smooth peaks and troughs. Source under-curve shading is omitted.
spec.mathematics: Empirical height data over 72 hours, reconstructed from source positions using cubic segments rather than a regular sine function. Heights range approximately from 0.4 m to 1.6 m. Successive highs or lows are approximately 12 hours apart.
spec.answerVisibility: The complete supplied chart is permanently visible; no answer annotations are added.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How many low tides occur in a day?

answer.worked: Each day has two troughs, so there are 2 low tides.

children.label: b
children.prompt: How many high tides occur in a day?

answer.worked: Each day has two peaks, so there are 2 high tides.

children.label: c
children.prompt: What word is used to describe graphs of this shape?

answer.worked: Sinusoidal: the smooth wave shape resembles a sine or cosine curve.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Estimate the low tide height and high tide height for Sunday between noon and midnight, to the nearest 0.1 m.

answer.short: Low tide: approximately $0.4\text{ m}$; high tide: approximately $1.6\text{ m}$.
answer.worked:
Read the trough near Sunday 3 pm and the peak near Sunday 9 pm from the height axis.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Low tide height}&\approx0.4\text{ m}\\\text{High tide height}&\approx1.6\text{ m}\end{align*}$$

children.label: e
children.prompt: Estimate the period for the tide graph, to the nearest hour.

answer.short: Approximately 12 hours, measured between successive peaks.
answer.worked:
Successive high tides occur at about 9 am and 9 pm.
$$\text{Period}\approx12\text{ hours}.$$
